newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA BLACK GROUP BUYS INTO NEW CLICKS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA BLACK GROUP BUYS INTO NEW CLICKS.

text.p: A South African black grouping based in the Western Cape on Thursday said it had bought a 10 percent stake in retailer New Clicks Holdings Ltd for 100 million rand.
Sancino (Projects) Ltd has purchased the stake from the Sanlam group, which sold 25 million New Clicks' shares at four rand a share.
The deal, which was financed by the Sanlam Development Fund, follows New Clicks' unbundling from former 51 percent majority shareholder Malbak Ltd .
The unblundling saw Malbak's holding in New Clicks distributed to its shareholders, the largest of which was Sanlam with an approximate 27 percent stake.

Sanlam, an unlisted South African insurance and financial services giant, has also sold seven percent of its New Clicks' shares to the Public Investment Commissioners (PIC), whilst retaining the balance of shares.
Sancino, formed 18 months ago, is a black empowerment consortium with 250 Western Cape-based members. It has existing investments in Channel Six Broadcasting and Grand Parade Investments.

New Clicks' chief executive Trevor Honneysett said a major implication of the unbundling from Malbak was that there was no majority shareholder for the first time in the history of the New Clicks group.
"We are truly on our own two feet now and relish the prospect of growing the business for the benefit of all stakeholders," Honneysett said.

He added that the group expected to meet its earnings forecast for the August year end. Announcing its half year results in April New Clicks forecast earnings growth of between 20 and 25 percent for the full year.

The PIC in April announced that it had acquired a 2.9 percent stake in New Clicks investing 33.8 million rand in the firm following an offer to Malbak minorities for their shares. It also bought stakes in other listed firms unbundled from Malbak.
